subject: Air-gapped release: offline image signing & update SOP
body:
From: John Doe <john.doe@acme-medical.com>
To: soojin_lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Security Team <security@acme-medical.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Request: air-gapped update process + artifacts

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. As discussed, Acme needs a formalized procedure for performing offline (air-gapped) updates to their on-prem Redwood Private nodes. The security team asked for the following deliverables before we schedule an onsite update window:

- A step-by-step SOP for image transfer and installation (courier/USB process)
- Signed image artifacts and a verification script we can run in an air-gapped environment
- SBOM and attestations for the release build
- Guidance on discrete rollout steps and rollback criteria
- Chain-of-custody and acceptance test checklist for the ops team

Can you confirm whether Redwood supports GPG-signed images and whether signatures can be produced via HSM (we prefer hardware signing)? Also: expected lead time to generate artifacts and a proposed validation window.

Appreciate it,
John

--
John Doe
Director of Infrastructure
Acme Medical Devices

---

From: soojin_lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: John Doe <john.doe@acme-medical.com>
Cc: Vendor Ops <vendor-ops@trusted-images.io>
Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2026 11:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: air-gapped update process + artifacts

John —

Thanks for the clear list. We can absolutely provide the artifacts and an SOP. Attaching a draft checklist to start (redwood-offline-release-checklist.pdf). High-level answers to your questions below, and I’ve looped in Dev and Marissa to add technical and deployment-review details.

- Signing: our standard practice is to produce an image manifest that includes SHA256 checksums and a detached GPG signature (we can sign via our HSM-backed signing service or provide a GPG-signed manifest if you need an offline-friendly format).
- Verification: we’ll supply a small verification tool (Python + static binary) that runs in an air-gapped environment and checks checksums + signature. The tool will accept either the HSM attestation token or a PGP signature file and public key.
- SBOM: we’ll export CycloneDX (CSV + JSON) for the build; see attached sbom-acme-20261105.csv.
- Chain-of-custody: draft steps included in the checklist — recommended courier tamper-evident packaging, and a two-person verification to open media on site.

Estimated lead time: 3 business days to generate artifacts and sign with HSM (assuming the release build is final). If you require manual code-signing keys provisioned to your KMS, add 5–7 business days for key exchange and approval.

Next steps: Dev will outline the exact signing commands and a verification script. Marissa will review rollback policy and acceptance tests. Once we have the signed manifests and verification script, we can propose a 2-hour validation window for your ops team.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Product Security Program Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-offline-release-checklist.pdf (PDF, 1 page)

From: dev_patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: soojin_lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, John Doe <john.doe@acme-medical.com>
Cc: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Vendor Ops <vendor-ops@trusted-images.io>
Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2026 13:28:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: air-gapped update process + artifacts

Folks —

Technical bits on signing and verification (implementation proposal):

1) Build output and artifacts
   - release-image.tar.gz (container files + runtime artifacts)
   - signed-image-manifest.json (fields: image_name, version, sha256, size, sbom_ref)
   - sbom-acme-20261105.csv / .json (CycloneDX)

2) Signing approach (two options)
   - HSM-attested signing: our signing service signs the manifest and returns an attestation blob signed by the HSM key (PKCS#7). The attestation includes a timestamp and certificate chain. Suitable when you can verify the attestation with Redwood CA certs we provide.
   - Detached PGP signature: we also emit a .sig file created with our GPG key. We will export the public key (gpg-public-keys.asc) for offline verification.

3) Verification script (air-gapped friendly)
   - verify_release.py (Python 3.10, single-file; includes embedded fallback binary for environments without pip)
   - Steps the script performs: 1) verify signature (GPG or verify PKCS#7 using supplied CA cert), 2) compute and compare SHA256 checksums of image layers, 3) validate SBOM matches manifest, 4) run a basic integrity smoke test (extract and assert runtime binary checksums).

4) Transfer media recommendations
   - Use write-once encrypted USB (hardware-encrypted) or courier with tamper-evident seals. Record serial numbers and include checksum manifest on a separate medium (paper or QR).
   - Two-person acceptance before connecting to the private network; perform verification on an isolated jump host with no internet.

5) Rollback and fallback
   - Keep last-known-good image and manifest on the isolated jump host. If verification fails or health checks fail post-install, revert to last-known-good and open a support ticket (OPS-3124).

Commands (examples):
   - Generate manifest: sha256sum release-image.tar.gz > release-image.sha256
   - Sign (GPG): gpg --output signed-image-manifest.json.sig --detach-sign signed-image-manifest.json
   - Verify (GPG): gpg --verify signed-image-manifest.json.sig signed-image-manifest.json

I can produce the verify_release.py and a statically-linked verification utility by EOD tomorrow for your test.

- Dev

From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: soojin_lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, dev_patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, John Doe <john.doe@acme-medical.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2026 15:46:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: air-gapped update process + artifacts

Thanks, all. A few deployment-review / operational items to lock down before we sign off on the SOP:

- Acceptance tests (run on isolated jump host, pass criteria):
  * service process starts within 90s
  * nightly job schedule loads and runs a dry-run of batched requests
  * token-level billing / counters reset verification (sanity check only)
  * end-to-end inference smoke test using local test vectors (results must match baseline within tolerances)

- Rollout plan (in phases):
  1) Validation on a single staging node using the verification script (2 hours)
  2) Canary roll to 10% of nodes (monitor latency/error spikes for 24h)
  3) Ramp to 50% (monitor for 72h)
  4) Full rollout if no regressions; otherwise rollback to last-known-good

- Chain-of-custody: courier manifest must include courier company name, tracking, pax who received package (ops engineer), time/date, and photos of tamper seal. Store photos in your audit repo and share link over DocuSign/Drive (redacted for PHI).

- Testing window: prefer weekday morning PST to align with Redwood on-call. We can provide a Redwood engineer to be onsite remotely during validation.

Marissa
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

Marissa / Team —

This is excellent and much appreciated. A couple of follow-ups:
1) Can you produce both HSM-attestation and detached PGP signatures? Security wants both for audit redundancy.
2) Please include a small hardened verifier binary in addition to the Python script — our on-prem engineers prefer minimal runtime surfaces.
3) Can we push the validation window to Tue 11/10 at 10:00 PST? That gives our procurement time to arrange courier and our compliance team to pre-approve the chain-of-custody template.

If you can confirm those three items, we’ll proceed with the procurement and schedule the courier.

Thanks,
John

Schedule: delivering artifacts and keys to Acme ops by Mon 11/9 EOD PST; validation window Tue 11/10 10:00 PST works for Redwood. I’ve created an internal ticket OPS-3124 and linked the checklist / artifacts (see related_links).

We’ll also provide a short runbook for on-site ops to follow step-by-step during the jump-host verification.

Thanks everyone — we’ll send confirmation once artifacts are staged.

Soojin Lee
Product Security Program Manager
Redwood Inference
